Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

commit adultery verb

also be unfaithful, cheat on (a husband or wife), have an affair, sleep with another man’s wife

classical

Suet. Aug. 67: mātrōnās (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Matt. 5.32: quī dīmissam dūxerit, adulterat (Lewis & Short)

adulterō, adulterāre, adulterāvī, adulterātum

verb, first conjugation

commit adultery; with an object, seduce (another man’s wife); also falsify, adulterate

From adulter. Cicero has the infinitive among things base to do but not indecent to name: latrōcinārī, fraudāre, adulterāre (Off. 1, ch. 35, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • moechor, moechārī, moechātus sum — commit adultery

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Catull. 94.1 (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.2.49 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētārum: Catull., Hor., Mart.)

    From moechus. Poetic and late (Lewis & Short).

  • moechissō, moechissāre — have one’s way with (a woman), as an adulterer

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 976: dum moechissat Casinam

    (Plaut. semel)

    A comic formation on moechus, found once; Lewis & Short renders it “ravish”.

Examples

  • quī dīmissam dūxerit, adulterat

    whoever marries a divorced woman commits adulteryVulg. Matt. 5.32 (Lewis & Short)

See also adultery, adulterer, screw.
